title: Mimi's Big Farm Sleepover
markdown:
Mimi the mouse arrived at Clover the cow’s farm with her whiskers twitching and her little traveling bundle no bigger than a walnut. The farm stretched wider than any burrow she had ever known. Hills rolled away in every direction, and the barn roof sat so high it seemed to hold up a piece of the sky. As the sun settled behind those hills in soft pinks and mellow oranges, Mimi felt a flutter that was half adventure and half oh, this is all so new.

Clover blinked her large, gentle brown eyes. Welcome, little Mimi, she rumbled, her voice as low and slow as earth settling for the night. Come. I will show you the lovely things before it is time to rest. The tiny mouse and the very big cow walked the barnyard together. Mimi’s paws tiptoed over smooth stones that felt like cool plates. She craned her neck at golden hay stacked in clouds that nearly reached the rafters. Each rustle sounded like a secret being tucked in. Plump sheep were already folding themselves into naps. Sleepy chickens hopped, one by one, onto their roosts and tucked their heads. The whole farm seemed to move at a calm, unhurried pace, as if nobody was in a hurry to be anywhere but here.

When the sky turned velvety blue and the first stars came out like scattered diamonds, Clover led Mimi into the barn. This is my favorite place to rest, little one, Clover murmured, and she settled with a sigh that made the sweet hay tremble under Mimi’s paws. Moonlight poured through the wide windows in long white ribbons. Shadows swayed on the walls. Mimi looked and looked. It was vast. It was quiet. It was nothing like her tiny burrow, where every corner knew her name. For a moment she wished for her own small bed, perfectly mouse-sized, with the ceiling close enough to touch.

Then Clover breathed out again, slow and deep, a sound so calming it might have been a lullaby made of grass. Mimi’s nose gave a happy little wiggle. The farm’s coziness was a different shape, that was all. A grand embrace. As big as a meadow, and just as kind.

She snuggled into a warm patch of hay right against Clover’s enormous soft flank. The air smelled of straw and milk and evening. Clover’s quiet breaths went moo-moo, moo-moo, as steady as a rocking chair. Straw shuffled. Far away, crickets sang. It was not the small contained warmth of a mouse hole. It was a spacious, peaceful warmth, like a giant fluffy blanket with room left over for dreams. Mimi listened to the rise and fall of that great gentle breathing until her own little heart matched it. Her eyelids grew heavy. Moonbeams, sweet hay, and Clover’s rumbling lullaby filled her mind, and everything felt perfectly, wonderfully right.
